records.name: Unicode Code Point vs UTF-16 Code Unit String Indexing
records.code_unit_size: Variable (1-4 bytes for UTF-8; 2 or 4 bytes for UTF-16)
records.indexing_semantics: Python 3 indexes strings by Unicode code points (characters). JavaScript and Java index strings by 16-bit UTF-16 code units.
risks: Characters outside BMP (such as emojis or rare CJK ideographs) take 1 index position in Python, but 2 index positions (surrogate pair) in JavaScript and Java
String slicing `s[0:1]` in JS slices half of a surrogate pair, resulting in an unprintable isolated high surrogate character
records.migration_notes: When migrating Python string indexing to JavaScript, use `Array.from(str)[i]` or iterator protocols to access code points rather than raw index `str[i]`.

records.name: Unicode Normalization Forms (NFC Canonical Composition vs NFD Decomposition)
records.indexing_semantics: Visually identical characters (e.g. 'é' as U+00E9 vs 'e' + U+0301 combining acute) compare unequal without normalization
risks: Database string equality lookups or hash map lookups fail when source data comes from macOS (NFD) and target operates in NFC
records.migration_notes: Use `unicodedata.normalize('NFC', text)` in Python when comparing strings from external systems.

records.name: Locale-Sensitive Casing (The Turkish I Problem)
records.indexing_semantics: Standard lower() / upper() assume English/Latin rules where 'I'.lower() -> 'i'. In Turkish, 'I'.lower() is 'ı' (dotless i).
risks: Security vulnerabilities or syntax errors when lowercasing protocol keywords (e.g., 'HTTP' -> 'http' or 'SELECT' -> 'select') in Turkish locale
records.migration_notes: Use ASCII-invariant casing or explicit invariant culture for protocol and keyword parsing.
